entry_state: Debt payment schedules differ from carrying values and change with fees and day-count conventions. Modification,derecognition and default require separate evidence. Conversion offers,amendments,discharge and delivery may occur on different dates. Cash-flow hedge reserves use cumulative values and release according to the hedged item's treatment,not derivative settlement alone. Fair-value hedge adjustments alter debt and require recalculated interest;benchmark reform has specific conditions. Excluded option time value is introduced on page204,with its method continuing next.
exit_state: Option protection cost follows transaction or time-period treatment,with actual and aligned components separately valued. A purchased call's cumulative-loss selector does not cover every signed collar. A matched zero-cost collar retains separate gross contracts and signed interim reserves,while terminal cost is clipped between its strikes. Forward-component treatment requires an explicit election. Rebalancing preserves old gains and layer origins;repeated additions never restart the cumulative lower-of calculation. Added and removed instruments remain the next dependency.

findings.observation: Protection premium,aligned intrinsic exposure and time-value mismatch are distinguished with complete cash/equity/inventory bridges. The balanced wrong-risk alternative makes the accounting consequence of copied option features visible.

The collar explicitly limits its matching assumptions and treats terminal-price weights as separate consistency witnesses,not a forecast. Rebalancing derives layer-specific cumulative changes and shows that a reset can balance while giving the wrong reserve.
